heading: Flight fare analysis findings: Booking early can save you big, last-minute flights cost 25% more on average; get cheaper fares by planning 30 days in advance
author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Sep 21, 2026, 19:28 IST
paragraphs: NEW DELHI: Everyone knows a last-minute flight costs more

Almost nobody knows by how much, or on which routes it matters enough to change what you do.An analysis of fares by the TOI-DPA Airline Price Index, flights across 54 routes connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune puts a number on it
Booking a month ahead instead of the day before saves about a fifth of the fare on the average route

And there is not one route in the set where leaving it late works out cheaper.Flying to Kolkata for Durga Puja? Be ready to pay 71% more on Oct 16What does the curve look like?The tracker sets the day-before fare on each route at 100 and measures every other booking point against it
A reading of 80 means a ticket bought at that point costs 80% of what the same seat costs the day before departure.Across the whole network the reading at 30 days out is 80

So the last three weeks before departure account for most of the damage, and the final week alone adds about 12 points.Read the other way, a passenger booking the day before pays roughly 25% more than one who booked the same journey a month earlier.Is there any route where waiting works?No
Not one of the 54.At 30 days out, every single route sits below 100, meaning every single route is cheaper booked a month ahead than booked the day before
The same holds at a week out and at two months out
The figures were checked on two consecutive captures and did not change.The closest any route comes to breaking even is Bengaluru to Chennai at 97, where booking a month ahead saves under 3%

The furthest is Ahmedabad to Pune at 45, where the day-before fare is more than double.Where does waiting hurt most?Ahmedabad to Pune is the worst in the country, at 121% extra for booking the day before

Kolkata to Chennai follows at 113%, then Kolkata to Bengaluru at 93% and Kolkata to Hyderabad at 90%.Route30-day indexExtraAhmedabad to Pune451.21Bengaluru to Hyderabad590.7Kolkata to Ahmedabad670.49Delhi to Hyderabad750.33Chennai to Pune790.26Bengaluru to Kolkata830.2Pune to Bengaluru850.17Delhi to Mumbai900.11Chennai to Bengaluru920.09Bengaluru to Chennai970.03At the other end the numbers collapse
Bengaluru to Chennai charges 3%, Mumbai to Delhi and Pune to Delhi around 7%, Chennai to Bengaluru and Bengaluru to Delhi about 9%.The gap between the two ends is the useful part
On a Kolkata route, planning ahead is worth more than the ticket itself

On Bengaluru to Chennai, planning ahead buys you a seat and almost nothing else.Why is Bengaluru to Chennai so flat?It is the shortest hop in the set at about 270 km, and it is well served, with roughly ten flights a day in each direction.Short, dense, heavily served routes tend to run something close to a fixed price ladder
There are enough seats that airlines are not squeezing the last few, and the flight is cheap enough to operate that the gap between a cheap seat and an expensive one is narrow in absolute terms
The result is a fare that barely moves as the date closes in.That is a convenience, not a bargain
It just does not get more expensive if you turn up late.So when should you book?About a month out, and there is a reason not to go much earlier.Thirty days is where the curve bottoms
At 60 days the reading rises to 82, and at 90 days to 86
Booking three months ahead costs slightly more than booking one month ahead on most routes

On six routes, including Mumbai to Delhi and Ahmedabad to Mumbai, the 90-day fare is actually a little higher than the day-before fare.Route by route, 34 of the 54 are cheapest at 30 days, 14 at 60 days and only six at 90.If you can plan one thing, plan to be booked about four weeks out
Earlier than that buys you certainty rather than savings
Later than that is where the money goes.Is there an exception right now?Yes, and it is a large one
Flights into Kolkata are currently running backwards.The median fare into Kolkata for a departure a week away is Rs 8,259
For a departure a month away it is Rs 14,117, which is 71% higher
Everywhere else the median goes the normal way, Rs 6,476 for next week against Rs 6,270 for next month.The reason is the calendar
A month from the capture date is Durga Puja week, when Kolkata fills up
So on those routes, for that week only, booking further ahead does not help because the date itself is the expensive thing.This is the exception that proves the rule rather than breaking it

It is the destination date that is dear, not the lateness of the booking.What this means in rupeesOn the morning of 16 September, across the 40 routes that touch neither end of Kolkata, the median advertised fare was Rs 6,957 for a seat the next day and Rs 6,270 for a seat a month out.That is a smaller gap than the percentage figures above imply, because the two are measured differently
The percentages come from the tracker's own fare-time index, which is built over a longer window; the rupee figures are a single morning's quotes

Treat the percentages as the shape of the market and the rupees as an illustration of one day.About this dataThe figures come from fares and schedules listed on the TOI-DPA Airline Price Index for 54 routes between Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune, captured daily
The percentage comparisons use the tracker's fare-time index, which fixes the day-before fare at 100 for each route and expresses the other booking points against it

Rupee figures come from the captures of 16 and 17 September 2026.LimitsThese are advertised medians, not fares any passenger finally paid, and a quote visible one morning can move.This is not the same as following one flight
The comparison is between what different departure dates cost when quoted on the same morning, not what one specific flight cost as its date approached

Those two things usually point the same way, and here they do, but they are not the same measurement.Flight counts move a lot between captures, so the description of how busy a route is should be read as approximate rather than exact.The TOI-DPA Airline Price Index aggregates fares from airlines and booking sites, so a figure here may differ from what an airline shows on its own website

The data records which airlines fly a route but not which airline charged a given fare, so nothing here identifies who sets these prices.TOI-DPA Airline Price Index is a joint initiative of The Times of India and Decimal Point Analytics.Source: Decimal Point Analytics Airline Price Index
